info.name: RemapFX
info.comment: Provides pixel remapping; equivalent to feComponentTransfer in SVG.

description.p: The RemapFX class provides an implementation of the feComponentTransfer functionality in SVG.
Internally the pixel rendering process is implemented using pixel lookup tables. As such this particular effect carries minimal overhead compared to most other effect classes.

action.name: Draw
action.comment: Render the effect to the target bitmap.
action.prototype: ERR acDraw(*Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Width, DOUBLE Height)

input.param: The X position of the region to be drawn.
The Y position of the region to be drawn.
The width of the region to be drawn.
The height of the region to be drawn.

method.name: SelectDiscrete
method.comment: Apply the discrete function to a pixel component.
method.prototype: ERR rf::SelectDiscrete(OBJECTPTR Object, CMP Component, kt::vector<double> Values)

input.param: The pixel component to which the discrete function must be applied.
A list of values for the discrete function.

description.p: This method will apply the table function to a selected RGBA pixel component. A list of values is required with a minimum size of 1.

method.name: SelectGamma
method.comment: Apply the gamma function to a pixel component.
method.prototype: ERR rf::SelectGamma(OBJECTPTR Object, CMP Component, DOUBLE Amplitude, DOUBLE Offset, DOUBLE Exponent)

input.param: The pixel component to which the gamma function must be applied.
The amplitude of the gamma function.
The offset of the gamma function.
The exponent of the gamma function.

description.p: This method will apply the gamma function to a selected RGBA pixel component. The gamma function is written as C' = Amplitude * pow(C, Exponent) + Offset.

method.name: SelectIdentity
method.comment: Apply the identity function to a pixel component.

input.param: The pixel component to which the identity function must be applied.

description.p: Selecting the identity function for a pixel component will render it as its original value. By default, all pixels will use this function if no other option is chosen.

method.name: SelectInvert
method.comment: Apply the invert function to a pixel component.

input.param: The pixel component to which the function must be applied.

description.p: This method will apply the invert function to a selected RGBA pixel component. The function is written as C' = 1.0 - C.
This feature is not compatible with SVG.

method.name: SelectLinear
method.comment: Apply the linear function to a pixel component.
method.prototype: ERR rf::SelectLinear(OBJECTPTR Object, CMP Component, DOUBLE Slope, DOUBLE Intercept)

input.param: The pixel component to which the function must be applied.
The slope of the linear function.
The intercept of the linear function.

description.p: This method will apply the linear function to a selected RGBA pixel component. The function is written as C' = (Slope * C) + Intercept. Any slope is permitted; for example a slope of -1 with an intercept of 1 inverts the component. Results are clamped to the valid range of 0 to 1.

method.name: SelectMask
method.comment: Apply the mask function to a pixel component.
method.prototype: ERR rf::SelectMask(OBJECTPTR Object, CMP Component, INT Mask)

input.param: The pixel component to which the function must be applied.
The bit mask to be AND'd with each value.

description.p: This method will apply the mask function to a selected RGBA pixel component. The function is written as C' = C & Mask. This algorithm is particularly useful for lowering the bit depth of colours, e.g. a value of 0xf0 will reduce 8 bit colours to 4 bit.
This feature is not compatible with SVG.

method.name: SelectTable
method.comment: Apply the table function to a pixel component.
method.prototype: ERR rf::SelectTable(OBJECTPTR Object, CMP Component, kt::vector<double> Values)

input.param: The pixel component to which the table function must be applied.
A list of values for the table function.

description.p: This method will apply the table function to a selected RGBA pixel component. A list of values is required with a minimum size of 1.
If a single table value is supplied then the component will be output as a constant with no interpolation applied.

field.name: AlphaTransfer
field.comment: The alpha channel's transfer configuration. See RedTransfer.

description.p: -ERRORS- Okay: NullArgs: InvalidValue: The Type is unrecognised or a parameter used by the Type is invalid.

field.name: BlueTransfer
field.comment: The blue channel's transfer configuration. See RedTransfer.

description.p: -ERRORS- Okay: NullArgs: InvalidValue: The Type is unrecognised or a parameter used by the Type is invalid.

field.name: GreenTransfer
field.comment: The green channel's transfer configuration. See RedTransfer.

description.p: -ERRORS- Okay: NullArgs: InvalidValue: The Type is unrecognised or a parameter used by the Type is invalid.

Each channel of a RemapFX has a transfer function that maps the channel's input value to an output value. The RedTransfer, GreenTransfer, BlueTransfer and AlphaTransfer fields read and write the complete configuration of that function as a RemapTransfer structure. The function of every channel is IDENTITY by default.
The Type determines which of the other fields are used. In the following, C is the input value and C' is the output value, both in the range 0 - 1.

list.li: GAMMA: C' = Amplitude * pow(C, Exponent) + Offset.
TABLE: The Count entries of Values define a piecewise linear function over equal intervals, between which C is interpolated.
DISCRETE: The Count entries of Values define a step function of equal intervals, and C' is the entry of the interval containing C.
MASK: The 8-bit channel value is combined with Mask using a bitwise AND.

description.p: The result is limited to the range 0 - 1. The function applies to non-premultiplied channel values. When the effect's colour space is linear RGB, the red, green and blue functions apply to linear values; the alpha function is never converted. Fully transparent pixels are treated as transparent black before the functions are applied, so an alpha function can make them visible.

Writing this field validates the members used by the Type and discards the rest, so reading the field back returns zero for unused members. Each Values entry and each parameter must be finite, Count must be between 1 and 1024 for TABLE and DISCRETE, and Mask must be between 0 and 255. An invalid configuration leaves the channel unchanged. Reading the field returns a copy of the configuration that is allocated as a resource.
The SelectIdentity, SelectLinear and other Select methods offer an alternative means of configuring a channel.
